name: Bintauna
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Usup, Hunggu Tadjuddin. 2001. Struktur Bahasa Bintauna. Jakarta: Pusat Pembinaan dan Pengembangan Bahasa. xii+225pp (grammar; Google Books snippet only, not readable online).

sources.citation: Sneddon, J. N. & Hunggu Tadjuddin Usup. 1986. Shared sound changes in the Gorontalic language group: implications for subgrouping. Bijdragen tot de Taal-, Land- en Volkenkunde 142(4): 407-426.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online (also online with a university library login)
sources.note: p. 409: 'Bintauna (Bnt).. We are unaware of any publications on this language.' The only stress statement (p. 418 and n. 15) concerns Buol, Kaidipang and Gorontalo (penult, antepenult with paragogic vowel); nothing is said about Bintauna stress.

sources.citation: Lobel, Jason William. 2013. Philippine and North Bornean languages: issues in description, subgrouping, and reconstruction. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bintauna appears only in the Mongondow-Gorontalo pronoun tables and one lexical citation (obolò); no statement on Bintauna stress (only a general footnote, p. 287, that most languages of Mindanao 'and areas further south' have lost contrastive stress).

sources.citation: Usup, Hunggu Tadjuddin; J.A. Karisoh-Najoan; J. Sendewana-Runtuwene; S. Remrev-Hersanti; N. Panrelly-Adrah. 1996. Struktur Bahasa Bintauna. Jakarta: Pusat Pembinaan dan Pengembangan Bahasa, Departemen Pendidikan dan Kebudayaan. xiii+225 pp. ISBN 979-459-680-9 (= Glottolog ref 323096, there mis-dated 2001). downloaded from the Internet Archive 20240318191231 of repositori.kemdikbud.go.id/3849/1/struktur bahasa bintauna 241-page scan with scanned layer).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent. Sec. 1.3 Tujuan (printed p. 5 = PDF p. 20) lists '(5) tekanan' among the intended phonology topics, but Bab II Fonologi (printed pp. 9-30: phoneme inventory by minimal pairs, diphthong /ay/, contrastive long vowels /ii uu ee oo aa/, phoneme charts, clusters, distribution) contains no stress/suprasegmental section, transcriptions carry no stress marks, and the Bab V summary (pp. 153-154) says nothing about tekanan.

sources.citation: Merrifield, Scott & Martinus Salea. 1996. North Sulawesi Language Survey. Dallas: Summer Institute of Linguistics.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: SIL survey with Bintauna wordlists in phonetic transcription; stress marks on the wordlist would be the only phonetic evidence of stress placement if no description states it.

sources.note: The only other primary linguistic work using first-hand Bintauna data (by the same author); comparative PGM reconstruction likely includes phoneme/stress notes for each daughter language, and Sneddon & Usup 1986 n. 15 shows the authors attended to stress in the group.
